name: sidebar
purpose: Application side navigation: a labelled <nav> with a list of links (buttons for items without an href) and nested groups that expand as disclosures (WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure Navigation). The active item carries aria-current="page". The sidebar can collapse to an icon rail whose labels are shown as tooltips, and below a viewport breakpoint it moves into a modal Drawer that the application opens from its own menu button. Activation emits a cancelable aui-navigate for client-side routers.
whenToUse: Primary or secondary navigation of an application with more destinations than fit in a top bar.
Hierarchical navigation with one or two levels of groups.
Layouts that need a compact icon rail on desktop and a drawer on small screens.
whenNotToUse: A handful of top-level destinations: use a top navigation bar or tabs.
Actions or commands (not destinations): use Menu or buttons.
Showing the current page's position in a hierarchy: use Breadcrumb.
Deep trees (more than three levels) or file-system-like hierarchies: use a tree view.
states: collapsed group containing the active item
responsive: Inline width is --aui-sidebar-width (default 16rem), or --aui-sidebar-rail-width in the icon rail. When the viewport is narrower than `breakpoint` CSS px (default 768; 0 disables), the <nav> moves into a modal start-edge Drawer (size sm) titled with the label, the host is display:none, and the application opens the drawer with open() or toggle(). Mode follows a matchMedia query on the viewport, not the container.
rtl: Logical properties throughout: the border sits on the inline-end edge, nested lists indent from the inline start. direction: 'rtl' sets dir="rtl" on the <nav> and the footer. The collapse chevrons are mirrored under :dir(rtl), rail tooltips open to the left in RTL (right in LTR), and the drawer opens from the right edge in RTL.
theme: Surface, border, hover, and selected role tokens. The active item uses color-selected background, color-selected-text, and semibold weight (not color alone). Forced-colors mode draws the active item in Highlight/HighlightText, disabled items in GrayText, and the border in CanvasText.
security: Labels are rendered with textContent, never parsed as HTML. Each href is parsed with the URL standard against document.baseURI; only http(s) and scheme-less URLs are accepted, otherwise SIDEBAR_OPTIONS is thrown without echoing the value. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. Active item, expanded groups, collapsed state, and mode live in memory and are reported through events; the application persists them if needed.

budgets.metric: Sidebar.create with 200 items in nested groups

performance.testedScale: 4 top-level items with a group nested two levels deep in the unit tests.

limitations: No arrow-key navigation between items; every enabled item and group button is a separate Tab stop.
The drawer breakpoint follows the viewport width, not the width of the sidebar's container.
The application must render its own menu button to open the drawer; the sidebar's collapse toggle is hidden in drawer mode.
The collapsed (rail) state applies inline only; it is ignored in drawer mode and forced to false when collapsible is false.
Disabled items get no rail tooltip, so in the icon rail they show only their icon or initial.
select() does not close the drawer; call close() after it.
Nothing is persisted; collapsed and expanded state reset when the sidebar is recreated unless the application passes them back.
unsupported: Rendering HTML strings or custom nodes in labels.
Hrefs with schemes other than http and https.
Groups that are also links (a group is a disclosure button only).
Badges, counters, or secondary actions inside items.
antiPatterns: Mixing destinations and commands in the same sidebar.
Marking a group as the active item (only non-group items can be active).
Rail mode without icons for most items (the first-letter fallback is hard to scan).
Handling aui-navigate with preventDefault but not calling select() afterwards, which leaves the previous item active.

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/sidebar: generated AuiSidebar directive ([auiSidebar] on an empty host); inputs mirror the options, outputs auiNavigate, auiChange, auiExpandedChange, auiCollapsedChange, auiModeChange.
